newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: INTERVIEW-Dhaka bourse chief warns kerb traders.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Dhaka bourse chief warns kerb traders.

text.p: The newly appointed chairman of the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) on Monday warned investors in Bangladesh's kerb market against acting on rumours, advising them to use brokers and to trade on company fundamentals.
"Trading on the kerb market is risky. They (investors) must trade through brokers," Abdul Huq Howlader, who replaced Imtiaz Husain as DSE chairman recently, told Reuters.
He said investors must check market rumours with the DSE, which regularly publishes information about listed companies.
Howlader said investors in the kerb market could not be protected by law. "Everybody should work within the law. Why should one go to the kerb market instead of the formal market?" he said.
Howlader was appointed DSE chairman on May 11 after the exchange's governing council dismissed Husain following a no-confidence motion by members.

The move by the council members came after Husain had been implicated by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in share-price manipulations that triggered upheavals in the stock market late last year.

The share market last week welcomed Howlader's takeover with investors and brokers viewing the change in leadership as a positive move by the exchange. The benchmark DSE index closed 44.88 points or 3.92 percent higher on Saturday to 1,189.46. Friday is the weekend in Moslem Bangladesh.
The exchange chief said people liked the change. "There was a need for change. There was no confidence when Imtiyaz Husain refused to resign," he said.
"In a complicated market you cannot expect solutions overnight. People's expectations are very high. They have burnt their fingers (as a result of price manipulations)."
"We must be very careful so that there will not be any more acts of price manipulation. The people should look into company fundamentals," Howlader said.
Thousands of investors in the kerb market lost their life savings when share prices dropped late last year after a steep rally from June to October.
The DSE index rose to more than 3,600 in early October from less than 1,000 a few months earlier. The index fell below 900 recently but has regained ground since Howlader's appointment.
The new bourse chief strongly rejected the idea that the DSE had been dogged by a lack of transparency in stock trading. "Let anyone prove it," he said.
"What sort of transparency do you want? We are transparent and we can prove it. There has been transparency in clearing, settlement on deals and trading on the stocks."
He said the country's laws should be changed so that a central depository system could be set up.
"I want to ensure fair trading on the floor," he said.
Howlader said there would be automated trading on the floor soon. "A foreign firm is working on the automation system. Hopefully it will be completed by the end of November."
